prompt: Why didn't Harvard have calculus classes when it first opened?
answer:
Harvard did not offer calculus when it opened in 1636 because calculus had not yet been developed in its modern form. Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz developed calculus independently in the late 17th century—roughly 50 years after Harvard was founded.

Early Harvard mathematics therefore focused mainly on subjects such as arithmetic, algebra, and Euclidean geometry. Calculus was introduced later; Harvard’s own history notes that mathematics had been taught there since 1638, while the study of calculus was firmly established in the 18th century, particularly through Professor John Winthrop.
